description:
## Goal

Write `test/filament/examples/inventory_test.exs` — tests for the Inventory example
from G3.

Two test groups:
1. **Rung 1** — `Inventory.Server` domain tests including the critical process-death
   → hold-release path
2. **Rung 2** — `CheckoutLineItem` component isolation: renders correctly for
   `{:held, token, item}` and `{:error, :insufficient}` hold states

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await
guidance. Do not improvise.

---

## 0. Prerequisites — read implementations first

Before writing any test code, read:

  - `examples/inventory/lib/inventory/item.ex` — Inventory.Item struct
  - `examples/inventory/lib/inventory/server.ex` — Inventory.Server
    handle_acquire/3 and handle_release/3 return shapes
  - `examples/inventory/lib/inventory_web/components/checkout_line_item.ex`
    — what props CheckoutLineItem takes, what it renders for each hold state

Also read `lib/filament/hold.ex` (from Track E, flm-zoc.1) to confirm:
  - `Filament.Hold.acquire/3` and `release/2` public API signatures
  - How `use_hold/3` communicates hold state to the component
    (is it via a hook slot message? what is the initial state on first render?)

The component uses `use_hold(assigns.server, assigns.item_id)` and renders based
on the return value. From the G3 spec, the hold states are:
  - `:uninitialized` — first render before hold acquired
  - `{:held, token, _}` — hold acquired successfully
  - `{:error, :insufficient}` — item unavailable
  - `{:error, :not_found}` — item id not found

---

## 1. Test file location

FILE: `test/filament/examples/inventory_test.exs`

`examples/inventory/lib/` is already in `elixirc_paths(:test)` from G3.

---

## 2. Rung-1 tests — Inventory.Server domain + process-death release

The critical test in this file is the process-death test: a holder process acquires
a hold, then dies (`:DOWN` fires on the server), and the hold is released automatically
without any explicit call.

```elixir
defmodule Filament.Examples.InventoryTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
  import Filament.Test

  # ── Rung 1: Inventory.Server domain ─────────────────────────────────────────

  describe "Inventory.Server" do
    setup do
      items = %{
        "item-a" => %Inventory.Item{id: "item-a", name: "Widget", available: 2},
        "item-b" => %Inventory.Item{id: "item-b", name: "Gadget", available: 0}
      }
      {:ok, server} = Inventory.Server.start_link(items: items)
      %{server: server}
    end

    test "acquire/3 decrements available and returns token", %{server: server} do
      # Filament.Hold.acquire/3 signature (from Track E, lib/filament/hold.ex):
      #   acquire(server, resource_id, subscriber_pid)
      # Returns {:ok, token} or {:error, reason}
      # Adapt if the actual signature differs.
      assert {:ok, token} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())
      assert is_tuple(token)  # token is {"item-a", make_ref()} per G3 spec
    end

    test "acquire/3 returns {:error, :insufficient} when available=0", %{server: server} do
      assert {:error, :insufficient} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-b", self())
    end

    test "acquire/3 returns {:error, :not_found} for unknown item", %{server: server} do
      assert {:error, :not_found} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "nonexistent", self())
    end

    test "release/2 restores availability", %{server: server} do
      {:ok, token} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())
      :ok = Filament.Hold.release(server, token)
      # Re-acquire to confirm availability was restored
      assert {:ok, _token2} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())
    end

    test "process death releases hold automatically — :DOWN fires", %{server: server} do
      # This is the core invariant of Track E: holds are released when the holder
      # process dies, with no explicit release call. The :DOWN monitor is set up
      # by Filament.Hold.GenServer when a hold is acquired.
      #
      # Spawn a holder process. It acquires the hold then blocks.
      # We kill it and assert the hold is released.

      # Confirm initial availability = 2 for "item-a".
      # Acquire one unit to confirm it decrements to 1.
      {:ok, _our_token} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())

      # Spawn a second holder. After it acquires, available=0.
      parent = self()
      holder = spawn(fn ->
        {:ok, token} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())
        send(parent, {:acquired, token})
        # Block indefinitely — hold is alive while this process lives
        receive do
          :stop -> :ok
        end
      end)

      # Wait for the second holder to acquire
      assert_receive {:acquired, _token}, 1000

      # Now kill the holder process — :DOWN fires on Inventory.Server
      Process.exit(holder, :kill)
      # Give the server time to process the :DOWN message
      Process.sleep(50)

      # The hold should now be released. We should be able to acquire again
      # even though we held one slot ourselves. Confirm by trying a third acquire.
      # (available was 2; we hold 1; holder held 1 → after death, back to 1 free)
      assert {:ok, _token3} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())
    end

    test "multiple holds on same item are tracked independently", %{server: server} do
      parent = self()

      holder1 = spawn(fn ->
        {:ok, t} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())
        send(parent, {:h1, t})
        receive do: (:stop -> :ok)
      end)

      holder2 = spawn(fn ->
        {:ok, t} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())
        send(parent, {:h2, t})
        receive do: (:stop -> :ok)
      end)

      assert_receive {:h1, _t1}, 1000
      assert_receive {:h2, _t2}, 1000

      # Both slots taken (available=0). Third acquire fails.
      assert {:error, :insufficient} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())

      # Kill holder1, one slot freed
      Process.exit(holder1, :kill)
      Process.sleep(50)
      assert {:ok, _t3} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "item-a", self())

      # Clean up holder2
      Process.exit(holder2, :kill)
    end
  end
```

## 3. Rung-2 tests — CheckoutLineItem component isolation

CheckoutLineItem calls `use_hold(@server, @item_id)` on mount. The hold state
determines what is rendered. Use a real Inventory.Server for these tests (there is
no HoldStub in Track F; use_hold is not stubbed via observable_stubs).

Read `checkout_line_item.ex` to confirm:
  - What is rendered for `:uninitialized` (probably loading spinner or nothing)
  - What is rendered for `{:held, _, _}` (probably "Add to cart" or checkout button)
  - What is rendered for `{:error, :insufficient}` (probably "Out of stock")
  - What is rendered for `{:error, :not_found}` (probably an error message)

```elixir
  # ── Rung 2: CheckoutLineItem component isolation ─────────────────────────────

  describe "CheckoutLineItem (rung-2)" do
    test "renders 'out of stock' when item has available=0" do
      items = %{"oos" => %Inventory.Item{id: "oos", name: "Scarce", available: 0}}
      {:ok, server} = Inventory.Server.start_link(items: items)

      # Mount the component. use_hold/3 will immediately try to acquire.
      # Since available=0, it gets {:error, :insufficient}.
      {:ok, view} = mount(
        InventoryWeb.Components.CheckoutLineItem,
        %{server: server, item_id: "oos"}
      )

      # Adapt the expected text to match the actual component rendering.
      text = render_text(view)
      assert text =~ "out of stock" or text =~ "Out of stock" or
             text =~ "unavailable" or text =~ "sold out"
    end

    test "renders checkout button when item is available" do
      items = %{"avail" => %Inventory.Item{id: "avail", name: "In Stock Item", available: 3}}
      {:ok, server} = Inventory.Server.start_link(items: items)

      {:ok, view} = mount(
        InventoryWeb.Components.CheckoutLineItem,
        %{server: server, item_id: "avail"}
      )

      # After mount, use_hold succeeded: {:held, token, _}
      # Adapt to actual rendered text
      text = render_text(view)
      refute text =~ "out of stock"
      refute text =~ "Out of stock"
      # Should render item name and some checkout action
      assert text =~ "In Stock Item"
    end

    test "two components competing for last unit — one gets held, one gets out-of-stock" do
      items = %{"last" => %Inventory.Item{id: "last", name: "LastUnit", available: 1}}
      {:ok, server} = Inventory.Server.start_link(items: items)

      {:ok, view1} = mount(
        InventoryWeb.Components.CheckoutLineItem,
        %{server: server, item_id: "last"}
      )
      # view1 holds the only unit

      # view2 — a new test process mounts and tries to acquire. Start it in a separate
      # process so it has a different pid (holds are per-pid).
      parent = self()
      spawn(fn ->
        {:ok, view2} = mount(
          InventoryWeb.Components.CheckoutLineItem,
          %{server: server, item_id: "last"}
        )
        # view2 should see {:error, :insufficient}
        text = render_text(view2)
        result = text =~ "out of stock" or text =~ "Out of stock" or
                 text =~ "unavailable"
        send(parent, {:view2_result, result})
      end)

      assert_receive {:view2_result, true}, 1000

      # view1 should still be held (render shows checkout action)
      text1 = render_text(view1)
      refute text1 =~ "out of stock"
    end
  end
end
```

      process-death release, multiple holds)
- [ ] Rung-2: all 3 CheckoutLineItem tests pass (out-of-stock, available, two-competing)
- [ ] `async: true` set (each test creates its own server, no shared state)
- [ ] No changes to example source files
- [ ] Full suite still passes: `mix test`
